note: The lower decks of the ship are dark and tiered like underground galleries.

anchor: like the prophet in the chariot disappearing in heaven and dropping his mantle to Elisha
note: In 2 Kings, Elijah is taken to heaven in a chariot of fire and drops his mantle, which Elisha takes up.

anchor: a diaphanous fleece of white furrowed vapor
note: Diaphanous: so light that light passes through it.

anchor: Suddenly eight bells was struck aft
note: Eight bells marked the end of a four-hour watch. At four in the morning the ship’s bell struck eight times.
source: W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “Bells”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000

anchor: the silver whistles were heard summoning all hands
note: Boatswains’ pipes were of silver and used to call the crew.

anchor: hatchways rimmed with racks of heavy shot
note: A hatchway is an opening in a deck. Racks held cannonballs around it.
source: W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “Hatchway”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000

note: Powder-boys carried gunpowder from the magazine to the guns in battle.
The break of the poop is where the raised stern deck ends.

anchor: the execution by halter of a military sailor was generally from the fore-yard
note: Halter: a hangman’s rope. Executions at sea were usually from the fore-yard.
source: W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “Fore-yard”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000

note: The main-yard is the lowest and largest yard on the mainmast.
The lee yard-arm is the one on the side away from the wind.

anchor: little or nothing of the perfunctory
note: Perfunctory: done as a routine, without real feeling.
Consummation: the end, the final act. Impended: was about to happen.
Penultimate: second to last, just before the end.

anchor: the ignominious hemp about his neck
note: Ignominious: shameful. Hemp: the rope of the noose.
Benediction: a blessing. A condemned man was expected to bless the officers.
A current of feeling passing through the whole crew at once.
Resonant: ringing out, resounding across the deck.
Voluminously: in great volume, with a swelling sound.

anchor: stood erectly rigid as a musket in the ship-armorer’s rack
note: The ship’s armorer kept muskets in racks.

anchor: the fleece of the Lamb of God seen in mystical vision
note: John the Baptist calls Jesus “the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.” Melville pictures a white sunrise like a lamb’s fleece.

anchor: took the full rose of the dawn
